fields.narrative_intro: *A doe-eyed person and a slack-jawed person discuss Gemini 4 Argon in an IKEA after closing.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
DOE-EYED PERSON: "Gemini 4 Argon tied for #1 on CWE-Bench cybersecurity."
fields.panel2:
[build]
SLACK-JAWED PERSON: "It beat GPT-6 Astra on Harvey Legal Agent, 19.6% to 5.4%."
DOE-EYED PERSON: "Its output window holds one million tokens."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
DOE-EYED PERSON: "It turns raw video into physics-accurate robotics simulation code."
SLACK-JAWED PERSON: "So the BILLY can assemble itself—and sue me?"
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: Both stare silently as a tiny robot assembles a BILLY; one-million-token instructions flood the showroom.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
DOE-EYED PERSON: "Enterprise deployments are 2.85x faster; Cartwheel cut tokens 90%."
SLACK-JAWED PERSON: "The robot uprising just hired a cost-cutting consultant."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A consultant's LinkedIn draft reads “BIGGER MODEL = BIGGER BILL”; the robot edits it to “2.85x FASTER, 90% FEWER TOKENS.”]

narrative_summary: A self-assembling IKEA BILLY turns Gemini 4 Argon's faster, cheaper deployment into a crisis for AI consultants' LinkedIn slogans.
rationale: Candidate 3 uses the story’s most distinctive facts—the BILLY, one-million-token window, Harvey benchmark, speedup, and token reduction—while giving them a sharper comic turn: the robot uprising hires a cost-cutting consultant. Its closing visual reinforces the joke instead of merely repeating the premise.
hat_pair: bucket hat with a tiny aquarium built into the brim
foam WiFi symbol worn as a glowing halo
